summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with inoperable cholangiocarcinoma and a history of recurrent cholangitis, was admitted with fever, chills, and nausea. He was started on empiric IV meropenem and vancomycin, though vancomycin was discontinued given negative blood cultures and low MRSA risk. Imaging revealed persistent cholangitis with pneumobilia limiting assessment, but no new biliary obstruction. Due to prior hemobilia, ERCP was deferred. A 10-day course of meropenem was planned via PICC line, with transition to oral doxycycline and Bactrim for infection suppression. His pancytopenia remained stable and within baseline. He improved clinically, remained afebrile, and was discharged home with home IV antibiotics and follow-up arranged with oncology and infectious disease.
